tagline: Scheduling links with overlay calendars and polished booking UX.
verdictSummary: A solo booking page for one calendar — read availability, show open slots, book, confirm — is a real weekend build. What takes it beyond a weekend is getting time zones, double-booking prevention, and reminder emails genuinely reliable, which is exactly the unglamorous work a scheduling tool actually gets paid for.
coreLoopDIY: A booking page for one calendar, reading Google Calendar free/busy, showing open slots in the visitor's own timezone, and creating the event with the guest invited.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay for a reliable scheduling experience that doesn't create friction or confusion for the guest — timezone handling and double-booking prevention are easy to get subtly wrong, and that's exactly where trust breaks.
notes: A good smaller-brand example: real open-source prior art exists, which makes the buildable case here more concrete than most.
prompt:
Build a solo booking page for one calendar: define a handful of link types (a slug, a duration, a buffer, allowed hours) in a config file. Read free/busy from one connected calendar via OAuth and show open slots for the next couple of weeks in the visitor's detected timezone, with a manual timezone switcher. On booking, collect the guest's name and email, re-check free/busy right before confirming (not just at page-render time) so two guests can never grab the same slot, then create the calendar event with the guest invited so the calendar app itself sends the invite. Send a confirmation email to both the guest and yourself, including a cancel link that removes the event.

Do not build team scheduling links, routing across multiple people, payment collection, or a reminder-email sequence — this is one calendar, one person, and getting timezones and double-booking genuinely right for that one case is already the real work.

faq.q: Can I import my existing SavvyCal link types and availability?
faq.a: Not automatically — there's no structured export of scheduling rules. Recreating a handful of link types and your availability windows is a short, one-time setup.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: The public booking page is fully responsive, so guests booking from a phone works fine. Editing link types is a config-file task, realistically done on a computer.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting and a domain, typically a few dollars a month — no per-booking or per-link fee.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: The polish that prevents booking friction. SavvyCal's overlay calendar and reminder sequence exist specifically to reduce no-shows and confusion; this build gets the booking right but doesn't chase the guest afterward to make sure they show up.
